previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain. She presented after an incomplete dialysis session with elevated potassium and blood glucose. Imaging showed stable moderate ascites, gallbladder wall edema, and findings suggestive of hepatic congestion likely due to cardiac etiology. A pelvic ultrasound ruled out an adnexal mass previously noted on CT. Her pain was managed conservatively, insulin regimen was optimized, and hyperkalemia resolved with dialysis. She improved clinically and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up in cardiology, gastroenterology, and endocrinology, along with a liver MRI to evaluate chronic congestion.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with T1DM, ESRD on HD (___), HTN, and 
multiple recent admissions for gastroparesis, admitted for 
recurrent abdominal pain and nausea subsequently diagnosed with 
congestive hepatopathy.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
==============

# Congestive Hepatopathy: Patient presented with diffuse 
abdominal pain and nausea, different from prior episodes of 
gastroparesis (notably, no vomiting). Patient has been noted on 
previous admissions to have ascites and transaminitis of unclear 
etiology. Diagnostic paracentesis during prior admission 
revealed a SAAG of 1.8 consistent with portal hypertension, CHF 
or Budd-Chiari syndrome. This admission, her abdomen remained 
distended secondary to ascites and was mildly tender to 
palpation diffusely. Repeat RUQ Ultrasound (___) revealed 
gallbladder wall thickening thought secondary to volume overload 
and third spacing, as well as a small amount of ascites and 
evidence of passive hepatic congestion (unchanged since her last 
RUQ ultrasound on ___. HIDA scan negative for acute 
cholecystitis.  During this admission, her transaminitis 
downtrended with removal of fluid volume with hemodialysis and 
dietary restriction. She tested negative for HBV (positive HBsAb 
only) and HCV and HAV. Also had a negative ___, AMA, and 
anti-smooth muscle antibody. Hepatology was consulted and felt 
data were most consistent with congestive hepatopathy secondary 
to heart failure in the setting of volume overload (last TTE 
revealed elevated PASP, RV dysfunction, RA dilatation, and 
reduced LVEF of ~45%). Discussion with her nephrology team 
revealed that they are performing the maximum amount of 
ultrafiltration possible within the time constraints of her 
dialysis sessions ___ per session). The patient was informed 
that the only way to reduce her abdominal pain and distention 
was to consume considerably less salt and fluid each day, and to 
maintain tighter glycemic control. She was also scheduled for 
cardiology follow up and should have a repeat echo to evaluate 
for persistence vs resolution of her RV dysfunction after 
implementing this plan.

# Hyperkalemia: Potassium was 6.0 on admission on ___, 
increasing to 7.0 by ___. No acute T wave changes. She 
received 10u insulin and an amp of D50 in the ED, then underwent 
inpatient hemodialysis on ___. She was monitored on telemetry 
until her serum potassium normalized with HD.

# Brittle T1DM: Labile blood sugars in past. Last HbA1c in ___ 
was 8.9. Hypoglycemic to 56 on arrival to ED, likely from poor 
PO intake. Given 1 amp of D50 and 10u insulin for combination of 
hypoglycemia and hyperkalemia (see above). Following 
hemodialysis on ___, she was started on her usual renal diet 
and her home insulin regimen was resumed.

# Code Status: FULL CODE  
# Emergency Contact: ___ (MOTHER, ___

==== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ====

# Outpatient GI f/u with Dr. ___ on ___ for ongoing 
management of her gastroparesis and counseling regarding 
congestive hepatopathy.

# Cardiology f/u with Dr. ___ on ___: please consider 
repeating TTE at that time to evaluate for RV recovery vs 
persistence of RV dysfunction.

# If patient is re-admitted with abdominal pain similar to prior 
episodes, volume removal with HD should be a priority, as well 
as more rigorous nutritional counseling regarding the importance 
of adhering to a low-salt diet and improving her glycemic 
control.

# Gabapentin might have worked well for pain relief for the 
patient (she got one dose and found good effect but this was 
also have fluid removal at HD) this may be considered as an 
alternative to narcotics.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ on ___ with persistent abdominal 
pain. During this admission, we determined that your abdominal 
pain is due to your body retaining too much fluid (specifically, 
your liver became swollen, an condition called ""congestive 
hepatopathy"". This is also the explanation for your 
swollen/distended abdomen. We are already removing the maximum 
amount of fluid at dialysis that we can ___ liters per 
session), but this is less fluid than you are gaining between 
dialysis sessions.

The way to eliminate your abdominal pain and distension is to 
reduce the amount of fluid and salt-containing foods that you 
consume on a daily basis. You also need to control your blood 
sugar as well as possible, since uncontrolled high blood sugar 
can also lead to fluid retention.  We have scheduled you for 
close follow up with several outpatient providers who will 
continue to assist you with these goals.

It was a pleasure to take care of you during your hospital stay.

Sincerely,
Your ___ Team

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ year old female with DM1 ESRD with ascites, distention,
diffuse abd pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound from ___ and CT from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. The contour of the
liver is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. Main portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow.  Pulsatile flow is noted in the portal veins. There is a
small amount of ascites.  To and fro flow is seen within the hepatic veins
suggestive of passive hepatic congestion.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER: Gallbladder wall thickening similar to prior exams is
nonspecific, and there are no gallstones.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 13.1 cm.

KIDNEYS: The right kidney measures 7.5 cm. The left kidney measures 7.9 cm. 
Bilateral renal cortical echogenicity is compatible with medical renal
disease. There is no hydronephrosis.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Gallbladder wall thickening is similar to prior exams and is nonspecific
which can be seen in the setting of third spacing.
2.  Small amount of intra-abdominal ascites.
3.  To and fro flow within the hepatic veins and pulsatile flow in the portal
veins are likely reflective of passive hepatic congestion.
4.  Renal cortical echogenicity bilaterally is likely reflective of medical
renal disease.
